overview: Selecting seats does SET seat:{show}:{seat} user NX EX 600 in Redis (atomic, auto-expiring hold). Checkout calls the payment provider with an idempotency key; on success a SQL transaction inserts bookings with UNIQUE(show_id, seat_id) as the final guard against double booking.

estimation.assumption: Illustrative opening: 100K clients competing for 1K seats.
estimation.calculation: 100,000 / 1,000 = 100 contenders per seat on average, with skew.
estimation.result: Popular seats create contention even when total database throughput looks sufficient.
estimation.implication: Use admission/waiting rooms, short hold TTLs and authoritative uniqueness constraints.

entityDetails.purpose: Authoritative seat ownership for a show.
accessPatterns: Check availability; hold and confirm selected seats.
constraints: A serializable transaction/row lock and unique seat booking are the final guard against double booking.
relationships: SeatHold covers show_id/seat_id rows; SQL retains authoritative confirmed ownership.

accessPatterns: Claim all requested seats; renew, redeem or release by owner/version.
constraints: Redis NX is per key: multi-seat holds need one atomic same-shard operation or rollback. Expiry does not authorize a late payment to steal a newly held seat.
relationships: show_id and seat_ids reference Seat; owner, version and expiry must still match at confirmation.

apiDetails.purpose: Hold all selected seats for a bounded time.
apiDetails.rationale: The hold must be all-or-nothing and tied to the authenticated owner.

apiDetails.purpose: Confirm a valid hold and payment.
apiDetails.rationale: Use provider idempotency and a durable booking state machine; compensate an authorization if the hold expired before confirmation.

steps.title: App → LB → Rate limiter → Booking Service → Seat holds (Redis)
steps.explanation: Rate-limit demand and atomically acquire all selected seats for the owner and hold version.

steps.title: Booking Service → Seat holds (Redis)
steps.explanation: Recheck current hold ownership and expiry.

steps.title: Booking Service → Payment gateway
steps.explanation: Authorize payment with a stable checkout idempotency key.

steps.title: Booking Service → Bookings DB
steps.explanation: Confirm under seat uniqueness constraints; void/refund if the hold became invalid.

steps.title: Booking Service → Booking events → Confirmation sender
steps.explanation: Send confirmation only after committed booking state.

failureCases.scenario: Payment completes after the hold expires
failureCases.handling: Recheck ownership and expiry transactionally before confirmation. If another user owns the seat, void/refund the first payment idempotently instead of double booking.

alternatives: Use SQL row locks when one authoritative seat-state transaction handles contention. Use Redis holds plus SQL uniqueness for heavier admission, accepting a fenced cross-store booking/payment state machine.
